anchorData:
PHENOMENON: A loaded mkokoteni (cart 50 kg + 5 sacks of maize at 50 kg each = 300 kg total) is released from rest (u = 0) at the top of a straight, steady section of the Limuru-Nairobi escarpment road. Slope: sin(angle) = 0.2 (about 11.5 degrees), so the vertical drop is 0.2 m for every 1 m travelled along the road. Ignoring friction and air resistance, constant acceleration along the slope a = g x 0.2 = 10 x 0.2 = 2.0 m/s² (mass does not change it). It crashes into a parked lorry after 100 m along the road, i.e. a vertical drop of 20 m.

MKOKOTENI TABLE (u = 0, a = 2 m/s², v = 2t, s = t²): t=0 s: v=0 m/s, s=0 m | t=1: v=2, s=1 | t=2: v=4, s=4 | t=3: v=6, s=9 | t=4: v=8, s=16 | t=5: v=10, s=25 | t=6: v=12, s=36 | t=8: v=16, s=64 | t=10 (CRASH): v=20 m/s (=72 km/h), s=100 m. Average speed over the 10 s = 100/10 = 10 m/s (=(0+20)/2). Check: v²=2as=2x2x100=400, v=20.

FREE FALL COMPARISON: a vertical drop of 20 m in free fall (a = g = 10 m/s²) takes t = sqrt(2x20/10) = 2 s and gives v = 20 m/s. The cart ends at the same 20 m/s but takes 10 s, because the slope only provides 0.2 of g. Free fall is the extreme case of a vertical slope (sin = 1, a = g).

L2 MATATU (Thika Road): u=0, a=1.5 m/s², t=8 s -> v=12 m/s, s=48 m.

L3 PROBLEM SET: (a) Rift Valley 400 m runner: from rest, a=4 m/s² for 2.5 s -> v=10 m/s, s=12.5 m. (b) Boda-boda before a police check: u=15 m/s, a=-3 m/s², stops (v=0) after t=5 s and s=37.5 m. (c) Ball thrown upward at u=+15 m/s from a Mombasa rooftop 20 m above the ground (up positive, a=-10 m/s²): rises 11.25 m more (max height 31.25 m above ground) in 1.5 s; returns to the ground (s=-20 m) at t=4 s; impact velocity v=15-10x4=-25 m/s (25 m/s downward).

L4 CLASS DROP DATA (drop height h = 2.0 m, three objects, mean of 5 trials each): rubber bung 0.63 s, stone 0.64 s, crumpled paper ball 0.65 s. Mean time 0.64 s. Estimated g = 2h/t² = 4/0.64² = 4/0.4096 = 9.8 m/s² (to 2 s.f.). Theory with g=10: t = sqrt(0.4) = 0.63 s. Differences are within reaction-time error. Exercises use g = 10 m/s².

L5 CALCULATIONS (u=0, a=g=10): (a) mango falls from a 5 m branch: t=1 s, v=10 m/s. (b) an object hits the ground at 30 m/s: dropped from h=v²/2g=900/20=45 m, falling for t=3 s. (c) the cart on the slope uses a=2, not 10: at s=25 m, v=sqrt(2x2x25)=10 m/s (t=5 s).

L6 STOPPING DISTANCES (matatu on Mombasa Road; reaction time 1.0 s; braking deceleration 5 m/s² on dry road, 2.5 m/s² on wet road). 36 km/h=10 m/s: reaction 10 m, braking 10 m (dry) / 20 m (wet), total dry 20 m. 72 km/h=20 m/s: reaction 20 m, braking 40 m (dry) / 80 m (wet), total dry 60 m. 108 km/h=30 m/s: reaction 30 m, braking 90 m (dry) / 180 m (wet), total dry 120 m. Doubling speed multiplies braking distance by 4; tripling it multiplies it by 9.

L7 GRAPH (cart): v-t graph is a straight line through the origin with gradient 2 m/s²; area under it from 0 to 10 s = 1/2 x 10 x 20 = 100 m. s-t graph is a curve (s=t²).
characters: Mzee Kamau: vegetable and maize seller whose mkokoteni (300 kg loaded) rolled away while he was helping a customer; nobody was hurt, the cart was destroyed. Achieng: bystander/witness who says 'it started slowly then flew'. Limuru-Nairobi escarpment road: the steep straight section of 100 m is used; at the bottom is a parked lorry. Mkokoteni: no engine, no one pushing, friction ignored. Matatu on Thika Road (L2) and Mombasa Road (L6). Boda-boda rider (L3, rider Otieno) braking before a police check. Rift Valley 400 m runner (L3, fictional; do not give real athlete data). Mombasa rooftop (20 m high, L3). Mango tree in a school compound (5 m branch, L5). Kinangop descent: signed steep road with warning signs (L6). NTSA: National Transport and Safety Authority, sets road-safety rules (L6, L7). Group research topics (L6-7): SGR train, pole vault, construction safety.
outcome: The released mkokoteni accelerates steadily at 2.0 m/s² down the escarpment because gravity pulls it down the slope all the time, so its velocity rises by 2 m/s every second: 4 m/s after 2 s, 10 m/s after 5 s, and 20 m/s (72 km/h) after 10 s and 100 m, when it hits the lorry. It starts slowly because velocity begins at zero, and it feels sudden because the distance covered grows as t² (25 m by 5 s, but 100 m by 10 s). Because the acceleration is constant, the equations of motion predict its speed and distance at any moment; free fall is the same physics with a = g = 10 m/s² on a vertical path, and the same equations show why higher speeds need much longer stopping distances.
conventions: Distance: total path length, scalar, metres (m). Displacement: straight-line change in position with direction, vector, m. Speed: distance/time, scalar. Velocity: displacement/time, vector. Acceleration a: change in velocity per unit time, m/s² (vector; negative = deceleration/retardation). Symbols: u initial velocity, v final velocity, a acceleration, s displacement, t time (SI units: m, s, m/s, m/s²). Convert km/h to m/s by dividing by 3.6. The FOUR EQUATIONS OF LINEAR MOTION (constant acceleration, given without derivation) are written exactly: (1) v = u + at; (2) s = ut + ½at²; (3) v² = u² + 2as; (4) s = ½(u+v)t. Do not call them 'SUVAT' in lesson text. Sign convention: choose the direction of motion as positive; for vertical motion UP is positive, so a = -10 m/s² for upward-thrown objects; for objects dropped from rest and measured downward, take down as positive with a = +10. g = 10 m/s² for all calculations (measured 9.8 acknowledged). Free fall: motion under gravity alone, with air resistance negligible. The mkokoteni on the slope is NOT free fall: its acceleration is g x 0.2 = 2 m/s²; never use a = 10 for the cart. Friction and air resistance are ignored unless stated. Use 'the equations of linear motion' as the formula name. Always state values with units; keep the cart figures exactly as in the table. DQB = Driving Question Board; model = annotated diagram plus velocity-time graph.

lessonMap.teaches: Precise definitions of distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration, and the claim that the cart's velocity keeps increasing (it accelerates); DQB launched
lessonMap.buildsOn: None (launches the phenomenon; uses prior Grade 9 ideas of speed)
lessonMap.usesData: Phenomenon description; average speed 10 m/s and acceleration 2 m/s² over 100 m / 10 s; qualitative speeds only (rises 2 m/s each second); 400 m lap for distance vs displacement

lessonMap.focus: Equations of linear motion: choosing the right equation
lessonMap.teaches: The four equations, the five variables (u, v, a, s, t) and how to select an equation by listing knowns and unknown
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1: the definitions of velocity and acceleration, and the cart's constant acceleration idea
lessonMap.usesData: Matatu on Thika Road (v=12 m/s, s=48 m); first rows of the mkokoteni table (t=1 to 5 s) as a check of v=u+at and s=½at²

lessonMap.focus: Problem solving with the equations, including deceleration and upward motion
lessonMap.teaches: Strategy for multi-step problems: sign convention, negative acceleration and motion thrown upward under a = -10 m/s²
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2: the four equations and the selection method
lessonMap.usesData: L3 problem set: 400 m runner, boda-boda braking, ball from Mombasa rooftop

lessonMap.focus: Investigating free fall: predict and observe
lessonMap.teaches: All objects fall with the same acceleration when air resistance is negligible, and g can be estimated from g = 2h/t²
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2 (s = ½at² with u=0) and Lesson 3 (sign convention)
lessonMap.usesData: L4 class drop data: h=2.0 m, times 0.63/0.64/0.65 s, mean 0.64 s, g estimate 9.8 m/s²

lessonMap.focus: Freely falling bodies: explain and calculate
lessonMap.teaches: Applying the equations with u=0 and a=g to free fall, and why the slope reduces the cart's acceleration to a fraction of g
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 4: g from measurement; Lessons 2-3: equations; Lesson 1: acceleration
lessonMap.usesData: L5 calculations (mango, 45 m drop, cart at 25 m) and FREE FALL COMPARISON (20 m drop gives 2 s, 20 m/s, vs cart 10 s, 20 m/s)

lessonMap.focus: Road safety: stopping distance and applications
lessonMap.teaches: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance, and braking distance depends on the square of speed (v²/2a)
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 3: deceleration problems with v²=u²+2as; Lesson 5: dangers of speed on slopes
lessonMap.usesData: L6 stopping-distance table (10, 20, 30 m/s; dry and wet), Kinangop descent signs, NTSA

lessonMap.focus: Group presentations and building the class model
lessonMap.teaches: Representing motion as a velocity-time graph: gradient = acceleration, area = displacement, linking all concepts into one explanatory model
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1-6 (all concepts; group research from Lesson 6)
lessonMap.usesData: L7 graph of the cart (gradient 2 m/s², area 100 m at 10 s) and the full mkokoteni table

lessonMap.teaches: No new content: individual synthesis and a written final explanation of why the cart keeps getting faster and how it can be predicted (gravity, constant acceleration, equations)
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1-7, especially the model from Lesson 7 and the DQB
lessonMap.usesData: Whole mkokoteni table (t=10 s, v=20 m/s, s=100 m), FREE FALL COMPARISON, L5 mango, a sprinter problem built like L3 (a), journal comparing with Lesson 1 predictions
